> Sub-question 2 (host column). The vaginal ring acts locally at the cervix;
> the injectable and the pill are systemic. If delivery route matters for the
> tissue, it should show in the women's own genes.
>
> Two things before any test: the group is defined from the **metadata**, so we
> are free to test it on the **gene table** (never both from the same table),
> and raw counts go into DESeq2 — never CPM, never logged.

```{r setup}
library(conflicted)  # make any name clash between packages a loud error
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)
library(patchwork)

# filter() is claimed by both dplyr and base R. We always mean the dplyr one.
# DESeq2's dependencies mask base R's set operations; the helper needs the
# base versions.
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::count,
                 base::setequal, base::setdiff, base::intersect, base::union)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

d <- read_counts("group_b")

# The group we test: ring against the two systemic methods pooled.
# 26 ring vs 67 systemic is our best-powered two-arm contrast (93 in total).
meta <- d$metadata |>
  mutate(systemic = if_else(arm == "ring", "ring", "systemic"))
```

## Order check first

DESeq2 matches count columns to metadata rows **by position, not by name** —
it will not warn us, it will just be wrong. The helper already reorders both
tables to `metadata$sample_id`, but we check rather than trust.

```{r}
identical(colnames(d$genes), meta$sample_id)
```

## Who is in the comparison, and is anything confounded?

Nobody was randomised. If BV, pH or STI differ between ring and systemic,
or the methods sat on different sequencers, any gene signal could be that
instead.

```{r}
meta |> count(arm, systemic)

meta |>
  group_by(systemic) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            bv_pos  = sum(bv == "positive"),
            mean_ph = round(mean(ph, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            sti_pos = sum(any_sti == 1))

table(systemic = meta$systemic, batch = meta$rnaseq_batch)
```

## The gene count table before testing

14,226 genes, most of them barely counted. DESeq2 cannot estimate a
dispersion for a gene that is zero almost everywhere, so we pre-filter: keep
genes with at least 10 reads in at least a quarter of the samples (24 of 93).
Same rule the workshop used on the instructional dataset.

```{r}
keep <- rowSums(d$genes >= 10) >= 24
sum(keep)
genes_kept <- d$genes[keep, ]
```

## Ordinate the genes before testing them

Same instinct as the microbiome doc: look at the structure first. CLR +
Euclidean (Aitchison distance) on the genes, coloured by the ring/systemic
group and then by BV — if BV dominates the picture again, we know what to
adjust for.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
library(microViz)
library(phyloseq)

ps_genes <- as_counts(dataset = "group_b", table = "rnaseq",
                      min_count = 10, min_samples = 24)

# ord_plot() reads variables from the phyloseq object's own sample data, so
# the ring/systemic group has to live there too.
sd <- as(sample_data(ps_genes), "data.frame")
sd$systemic <- if_else(sd$arm == "ring", "ring", "systemic")
sample_data(ps_genes) <- sample_data(sd)

ord_genes <- ps_genes |>
  tax_transform("clr", rank = "symbol") |>
  dist_calc("euclidean") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA")

p_ord_group <- ord_genes |>
  ord_plot(colour = "systemic") +
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = systemic), type = "t", linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "Gene PCoA, ring vs systemic", colour = NULL)
p_ord_bv <- ord_genes |>
  ord_plot(colour = "bv") +
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = bv), type = "t", linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "Same ordination, coloured by BV", colour = NULL)
p_ord_group + p_ord_bv
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
# And against the sequencer batch, the other thing that could be running axis 1.
ord_genes |>
  ord_plot(colour = "rnaseq_batch") +
  labs(title = "Same ordination, coloured by sequencing batch", colour = "batch")
```

## DESeq2: ring against the systemic methods

Raw counts in, DESeq2 does its own normalisation. The cross-tab above showed
the batch is balanced (13/13 ring, 34/33 systemic), so batch stays out; but
STI is lopsided (17 of 26 ring vs 31 of 67 systemic), so the design adjusts
for BV, pH and STI — the things an observational comparison must control for.

```{r}
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = genes_kept,
  colData   = meta |> as.data.frame() |> `rownames<-`(meta$sample_id) |>
    mutate(bv = factor(bv),
           # any_sti is coded 0/1; as a bare integer DESeq2 treats it as a
           # continuous variable and warns about it. For two values the model
           # is identical either way, but we say what we mean: a factor.
           any_sti = factor(any_sti),
           systemic = factor(systemic, levels = c("systemic", "ring"))),
  design = ~ bv + ph + any_sti + systemic
)

# poscounts size factors: the table has zeros, and the default geometric-mean
# estimator fails or distorts when genes are zero in many samples.
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = "poscounts")
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# How many genes did the size factors actually use?
length(which(rowSums(counts(dds) > 0) > 0))
summary(sizeFactors(dds))

res <- results(dds, contrast = c("systemic", "ring", "systemic"))
# Positive log2FoldChange = higher in the ring group.
summary(res)
```

## What came out

```{r}
res_df <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  rownames_to_column("ensembl_gene_id") |>
  left_join(d$gene_info, by = "ensembl_gene_id") |>
  mutate(symbol = coalesce(symbol, ensembl_gene_id))

res_df |>
  summarise(tested   = sum(!is.na(pvalue)),
            raw_p05  = sum(pvalue < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            padj_05  = sum(padj  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            padj_10  = sum(padj  < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE))

# With ~14,000 genes tested, 5% of 14,000 noise p-values is ~700 — that is why
# only padj counts, and why a raw-p histogram should be flat-ish with a spike
# near zero if anything is real.
res_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pvalue)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, colour = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 3) +
  labs(x = "raw p-value", y = "genes",
       title = "Raw p-values: flat means nothing, a spike near 0 means signal")

res_df |>
  filter(padj < 0.05) |>
  arrange(padj) |>
  select(symbol, gene_name, baseMean, log2FoldChange, padj) |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
# Volcano: effect size against significance. Red = padj < 0.05.
p_volcano <- res_df |>
  filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  mutate(sig = padj < 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), colour = sig)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey60", "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (positive = higher in ring)",
       y = "-log10(adjusted p)",
       title = paste0(sum(res_df$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
                      " genes at padj < 0.05, ring vs systemic"))

# Boxplots of the top six by padj, on the DESeq2 log scale (normalised, logged
# — this is a *look*, the test itself used raw counts).
top6 <- res_df |> filter(padj < 0.05) |> arrange(padj) |> slice_head(n = 6)
norm_log <- log2(counts(dds, normalized = TRUE) + 1)
pl <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(top6)), \(i) {
  sym <- top6$symbol[i]
  tb <- tibble(sample_id = colnames(norm_log), expr = norm_log[top6$ensembl_gene_id[i], ]) |>
    left_join(meta |> select(sample_id, systemic), by = "sample_id")
  ggplot(tb, aes(x = systemic, y = expr, fill = systemic)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "log2 norm counts", title = sym) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
})
p_box <- patchwork::wrap_plots(pl, nrow = 2)

p_volcano / p_box + patchwork::plot_annotation(
  title = "Ring vs systemic, host gene expression (Study B)")

# Save a copy for the group's slides.
dir.create(here("group_project/figures"), showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(here("group_project/figures/volcano-ring-vs-systemic.png"),
       width = 7, height = 9, dpi = 300)
```

## How much is the ring, really?

The top genes look like a list, but with three covariates in the design we can
ask how much of the ring-vs-systemic difference survives. A quick sanity check:
rerun with only `systemic` in the design and compare the two result tables.

```{r}
dds_bare <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = genes_kept,
  colData   = meta |> as.data.frame() |> `rownames<-`(meta$sample_id) |>
    mutate(bv = factor(bv),
           any_sti = factor(any_sti),
           systemic = factor(systemic, levels = c("systemic", "ring"))),
  design = ~ systemic
)
dds_bare <- estimateSizeFactors(dds_bare, type = "poscounts")
dds_bare <- DESeq(dds_bare)
res_bare <- results(dds_bare, contrast = c("systemic", "ring", "systemic"))

tibble(adjusted = sum(res    $padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
       bare     = sum(res_bare$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
       row = "genes at padj < 0.05")

# Do the two runs agree on which genes matter?
r1 <- res_df |>
  transmute(ensembl_gene_id, lfc_adjusted = log2FoldChange, padj)
r2 <- as.data.frame(res_bare) |>
  rownames_to_column("ensembl_gene_id") |>
  transmute(ensembl_gene_id, lfc_bare = log2FoldChange)
r1 |>
  inner_join(r2, by = "ensembl_gene_id") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = lfc_bare, y = lfc_adjusted)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "log2FC, no covariates", y = "log2FC, adjusted for BV/pH/STI",
       title = "Do the fold changes survive adjustment?")
```

## Interpretation

- **116 genes differ at padj < 0.05: 72 higher in the ring, 44 lower.**
  The headline is BPIFA1, a secreted innate-immunity protein of mucosal
  epithelium, ~64-fold higher in the ring (padj = 2×10⁻¹¹). Other up genes
  include SERPINA11 and CHGA; down genes include TGM3 and KPRP, both
  keratinocyte/epithelial structural proteins. The mix reads as epithelial
  barrier and secretory biology, which is exactly the tissue the ring
  touches.
- **The covariates matter: the bare design calls 227 genes, the adjusted
  one 116.** Nearly half the unadjusted list was BV, pH or STI talking —
  and STI is genuinely lopsided here (17/26 ring vs 31/67 systemic), so
  without adjustment we would have presented a method effect that is partly
  a who-chose-what effect.
- **The signal is real, not mass noise.** The raw-p histogram has a spike
  near zero over a flat background; 1,445 raw p < 0.05 is about double the
  ~700 the null would produce across 13,707 tests.
- **What we do not believe about our own result:** 26 ring samples is a
  small group for a whole-transcriptome contrast, and DESeq2 flagged 6
  outlier genes — BPIFA1's huge fold change should be shown as a boxplot
  (it is, below the volcano) and not just claimed. Fold changes beyond
  BPIFA1 and SERPINA11 are modest. And "the ring touches the tissue" is a
  story we brought to the data, not one the data proved; Thursday's
  enrichment step is what tests it properly.

## Choices made

- **Group defined from the metadata** (`arm`), tested on the gene table;
  alternative was deriving it from a count table, which would break the
  define-from-one-test-the-other rule.
- **Contrast ring vs systemic pooled** (26 vs 67) as the best-powered
  two-arm comparison; alternative was testing all three methods at once
  (`~ arm`), which answers a different question with less power.
- **Genes pre-filtered** to ≥10 reads in ≥24 of 93 samples; alternative was
  no filter, which wastes dispersion estimates on genes that are zero almost
  everywhere.
- **`poscounts` size factors** because the table has many zeros;
  alternative was the default geometric-mean estimator, which drops any gene
  with a zero from the factor and shifts the normalisation.
- **Covariates in the design** (`bv`, `ph`, `any_sti`) because the arms were
  not randomised — STI especially is lopsided (17/26 ring vs 31/67 systemic);
  alternative was the bare `~ systemic` run, which we keep side by side so the
  cost of adjustment is visible. Batch was cross-tabulated against the group,
  found balanced, and left out; alternative was to include it anyway, which
  costs a degree of freedom for nothing.
- **Adjusted p-value threshold 0.05** on ~14,000 tests; alternative was
  raw p < 0.05, which would call ~700 pure-noise genes significant.
- **Positive fold change means higher in the ring**; alternative was the
  reverse, which reads the same numbers backwards.
